co_monkey_house_the.blurb: The Monkey House is a steep gneiss wall in Clear Creek Canyon above Golden, just past the second tunnel and across the highway from the Wall of the '90s, of which it is effectively an extension. Seventeen routes are on offer, almost all bolted sport lines of roughly 50 to 85 feet. The difficulty sits firmly in the hard range: a couple of 5.10s, a handful of 5.11s, and a big cluster of 5.12s, topped by a few 5.13 and 5.14 tickets. The wall faces west toward north, so it catches evening light with some shade creeping in higher on the slope. Expect a short hike up a wash or small ridge from the roadside pullout, and a crowd of strong sport climbers.

co_industrial_wall_the_2.blurb: The Industrial Wall is the overhanging far end of the Mickey Mouse Wall on Eldorado Mountain, south of Eldorado Canyon near Boulder. Seventeen climbs here are nearly all bolted sport lines, with a single trad route mixed in. The steep, pocketed face has few sharp edges or crack systems, and the grades are demanding: roughly six routes in the 5.12s, seven in the 5.13s and a few in the 5.14s. The wall looks due south and soaks up sun for most of the day, though it cools quickly once the sun slips behind the mountain in the evening. Reach it by walking the trail toward Mickey Mouse Wall; it is the overhanging face on your right.

co_new_funtier.blurb: New Funtier is one of the gentler corners of the Ouray Ice Park, in the Uncompahgre Gorge, reached by heading uphill from the upper bridge on the same trail that leads to South Park. Seventeen ice lines mostly run 25 to 100 feet, many of them set up for top-rope or screw protection. Grades span a gentle WI2 up to WI4, with the largest share at WI4, and the ice varies from season to season with the water flowing. It tends to be less busy than the better-known walls and makes a sensible first day in the park. Descent is by rappel or the gully at the uphill end, which feels a bit more awkward than at neighbouring areas.
